name: Sa'id ibn al-Nadr al-Baghdadi
nameAr: سعيد بن النضر البغدادي، أبو عثمان، نزيل آمل جيحون
diedNote: Died at Amul on the Jayhun (Oxus) in 234 (Ghunjar, the historian of Bukhara, via al-Mizzi).
region: Baghdad, then Amul on the Jayhun
role: Teacher of al-Bukhari; used by al-Bukhari alone of the six

teachers.name: Abu al-Bakhtari Wahb ibn Wahb al-Qadi

students.name: al-Fadl ibn Ahmad ibn Sahl al-Amuli
students.nameAr: الفضل بن أحمد بن سهل الآملي

flags.label: Thin file
flags.detail: Al-Mizzi records only Ibn Hibban's listing and Ghunjar's death date; the Taqrib grades him reliable on that basis and on al-Bukhari's use of him. His whole dossier is small.

flags.label: Homonym
flags.detail: Not Sa'id ibn al-Nadr ibn Shubrumah al-Harithi al-Kufi (maqbul, ninth generation); Ibn Hajar notes that some confused the two (Taqrib 2407).

bio: A Baghdadi who settled at Amul on the Oxus and taught there; al-Bukhari, who heard him alone ("narrated to me"), is the only one of the six to use him. Few critics spoke of him, which is why his reliability rests on Ibn Hibban's listing and on al-Bukhari's trust. In hadith 335 he is the second shaykh, joined to Muhammad ibn Sinan by the ha' of transition, and Ibn Hajar observes that the wording of the hadith as printed is his.
